summary: The periodic health verdict has no consumer after the start: a RED verdict neither blocks entries nor alerts, although D102 says a DEGRADED verdict 'blocks new entries once enabled'.
expected: After enable, a health verdict that is not OK blocks new entries.
actual: The verdict is consulted once, at the end of the start sequence. Afterwards it is stored, journaled and logged only; db_writes, rest_error_rate and telegram_delivery have no second consumer.
impact: None now (Demo). On mainnet a process healthy at start keeps accepting CONFIRMs while REST calls fail or alerts cannot be delivered; the owner reading D102 believes health gates entries continuously.
evidence: health.py:358 `latest_verdict` has no reader in src (grep); wiring.py:1091-1098 the health task body calls kill_gate_tick_once only; execution/enablement.py guard reads only `_disabled`; DECISIONS.md:60 and :106 quoted in the lane file; 24-22-SUMMARY.md:74 admits it.
why_tests_miss: Tests cover the verdict and the start-time enable; none asserts a state change after a RED tick.
recommendation: Build a second automatic caller toward disable() with a DECISIONS row, or correct D102 and add a 24-DEFERRED row; alert when the verdict changes to NO_TRADE.
known_prior: KNOWN:24-22-SUMMARY.md:74; wrongly described in D102, absent from 24-DEFERRED

rule: T-24-24 failure isolation; D-03 stop in order
summary: A CancelledError leaving one task body cancels all 13 scheduler loops, and shutdown_in_order then re-raises it before any shutdown step; no journal row, no held marker, no ordered stop.
expected: One task's failure never touches the others; an unexpected scheduler end stops the process in order and holds with the marker.
actual: All loops are cancelled; shutdown_in_order raises at its first step (bot, stream supervisor, stream writes, service.drain, executor close skipped); the error passes every `except Exception`, so nothing is printed or marked and asyncio.run cancels in-flight tasks.
impact: Protection stepping, reconcile, scheduled cancel and alert delivery end silently; restart policy `no` leaves the process dead; the only signal is the external heartbeat (not observed on a host). The mechanism is confirmed; the trigger was not observed.
evidence: Probe P1: 'scheduler task done: True cancelled: True'; 'shutdown_in_order RAISED: CancelledError | steps run before it: []'. scheduler.py:239 gather without return_exceptions; scheduler.py:268 except Exception; runtime.py:497-500 step catches Exception; runtime.py:598-604 and 388-400 catch Exception.
why_tests_miss: Scheduler tests raise ordinary exceptions or cancel run() from outside; none raises CancelledError inside a body or feeds a cancelled scheduler task to shutdown_in_order.
recommendation: Treat a CancelledError in a body as a task failure when the loop task is not itself being cancelled; catch BaseException in the scheduler shutdown step; alert CRITICAL when the scheduler ends without a stop request.

summary: A supervision task that fails on every run (or hangs, except protection_step) produces one journal row, no alert, a green heartbeat, and the reconcile health checks keep passing from the last good report.
expected: A supervision task that stops working is visible through an alert, a failing health check or a red heartbeat.
actual: One LIVE_TASK_EVENT row per outcome change; only `stall` events alert and only protection_step has a stall bound; ReconcileObserver has no time so `reconciled` stays True; the liveness probe ignores task results.
impact: Reconcile is the backstop of the protection task; if it dies quietly nothing compares the exchange with the local state while every external signal stays green.
evidence: Probe P2: 200 failing runs -> journal events [('first_run','RuntimeError')], alerts 0. P3: observer fields ['_latest','_compared'], reconciled True. P4: stamp with every task FAIL -> live_liveness_problem None. wiring.py:1179-1183 notes the observer only after the tick returns.
why_tests_miss: Tests assert the journal contract (one row per outcome change); none asserts that a persistent failure reaches the owner.
recommendation: Alert at N consecutive failures; add the time of the last compared tick to ReconcileObserver and fail the check beyond about three intervals; fail --liveness while protection_step or reconcile_tick is FAIL; give every REST-calling task a stall bound.
known_prior: partly KNOWN:24-DEFERRED R-28 / 24-REVIEW IN-03 (liveness ignores task results only)

summary: A failed BOT step (one failed Telegram call at start) is a degrade, never retried: the process runs for its whole life in SAFE_MODE with no polling while the heartbeat stays green.
expected: A process without its operator channel holds visibly or keeps retrying the bot.
actual: BOT is not a hold step; start() is called once; after a failure there is no APPROVE, /status, /safemode_exit or /close, and in the start_polling branch the bot's HTTP clients are shut down so no alert can be sent. The liveness stamp stays fresh.
impact: With a flaky network, a start during a short Telegram outage yields a process that looks healthy from outside and is deaf (possibly mute) while it may supervise a restored position.
evidence: startup.py:185-187 HOLD_STEPS excludes BOT; startup.py:1043-1049; telegram_runner.py:171-204 (initialize outside the try, shutdown in the except); PTB 22.8 _bot.py:843-870 (one getMe), _updater.py bootstrap_retries default 0.
reproduction: Code trace: run.run(STEP_BOT) -> exception -> degrade -> SCHEDULER; _run_async waits on the stop event.
why_tests_miss: The start-sequence test asserts the degrade class of a failing step, not what the running process can still do.
recommendation: Owner choice: make BOT a hold step, or retry the bot start from a scheduler task and fail --liveness while the runner is not running.

summary: The reconcile tick is skipped for every symbol for as long as any placement task is alive; the skip has no upper bound although D097 states 'at most about two intervals'.
expected: A bounded pause of the comparison, for the symbol being placed.
actual: `if service.outstanding or service.take_settling(): return` covers all symbols and lasts for the whole life of the placement task; a task that never returns stops reconcile for good with no alert.
impact: With more than one symbol, a slow placement on one symbol suspends orphan sweeping, SAFE_MODE detection and pending actions for positions on the others.
evidence: wiring.py:1064-1071; execution_service.py:162-205 (`outstanding` = len(_tasks), tasks kept until done); DECISIONS.md:101.
why_tests_miss: tests/test_live_reconcile_settling.py pins the skip and does not bound it.
recommendation: Cap consecutive skipped ticks or exclude only the symbol in flight; journal each skipped tick.

summary: The live runtime never removes a held marker left by a killed hold; a later successful start of the same container is reported held for ever.
expected: A successful start clears a stale marker, as the paper runtime does.
actual: The only remove_marker call is in _hold's finally; after SIGKILL/OOM during a hold the marker stays and --liveness / --healthcheck report held while the process runs normally.
impact: A permanently red heartbeat on a healthy process (false alarm; alert fatigue).
evidence: Probe P4: 'the start was refused and this container is held (STARTUP_FAILED, exit 7)' with a fresh stamp; 'remove_marker call sites in src/live/runtime.py: 1'; held_marker.py docstring; paper/runtime.py:1691.
why_tests_miss: Live runtime tests cover a hold followed by a clean stop only.
recommendation: Remove the own marker in run_admitted once the start sequence is admitted.

summary: The probes and the admission-refusal hold use a cwd-relative state directory, while the running process anchors the same relative path at the repository root.
expected: The probe reads the directory the process writes.
actual: They agree only when the probe's cwd is the repository root; elsewhere the probe reports 'no liveness stamp'.
impact: Misleading probe output during manual diagnosis; none in the container (cwd is the root).
evidence: runtime.py:357 `state_dir: Path = args.state_dir`; config.py:268-272 `directory = repo_root / directory`; probe P5.
reproduction: Run --liveness from a directory other than the repository root while the process runs.
recommendation: Anchor args.state_dir once in main before both uses.

summary: D099 says every on-loop store call goes through StoreExecutor and nothing stays open; the protection coordinator, emergency closer, placement manager, SAFE_MODE controller, operator commands and scheduled cancel receive the raw synchronous stores and call them on the loop.
expected: No store call runs on the event-loop thread.
actual: The most time-critical paths block the single loop per database call, bounded only by the engine timeouts (lock 5 s, statement 10 s, connect 3 s, pool 5 s).
impact: In a database brown-out, stalls of seconds hit stop placement, emergency close, the stream keepalive and all tasks; the decision text tells the owner the matter is closed.
evidence: wiring.py:684-721, 747-761, 846-859, 1105-1113; protection.py:1406, 3202; manager.py:1230, 1323; safe_mode.py:519-536; DECISIONS.md:103; 24-DEFERRED R-08, R-23 name only part of it.
why_tests_miss: Composition tests use in-memory stores; nothing asserts the calling thread of a store call.
recommendation: Correct D099 and add a 24-DEFERRED row naming the coordinator, closer, manager and scheduled cancel; measure loop stall under a slow database in the Phase 25 soak.
known_prior: KNOWN in part: 24-DEFERRED R-08, R-23, R-10; wrongly described in D099
